name: Keep OpenAI prompts cacheable: stable text first
gain: OpenAI's words: cached input is "discounted up to 95%". On GPT-5.6 and later a read costs 0.1x input, 0.05x on GPT-6.1 Sol and Terra, and a write 1.25x for 30 minutes (vendor claim).
how: Caching is on by default, so nothing needs switching on. Put instructions and tools first and anything that changes last, then check the cached tokens in usage. Use the 12-hour lifetime only where requests are hours apart.
replaces: A changing value such as a date or user name at the start of the prompt, which stops the prefix matching.
trade_offs: On GPT-5.6 and later a write costs more than plain input, so a prefix that never repeats costs more.
A prefix needs at least 1,024 tokens on GPT-5.6 and later.
needs: Nothing new. PAT-prompt-caching-off does not detect this; show it only when the judge sees a changing value at the start of a long prompt.
usage_signal: Usage and Cost API: cached input tokens at or near zero on a model with large input

gain_model.formula: input_tokens * input_price * hit_rate * (1 - read_multiplier) - writes * input_price * (write_multiplier - 1)

test_recipe.what_to_compare: input cost and latency, identical answers

verify_rule: Cached-read share of input tokens on that model over 14 days

change_recipe.how: Caching is on by default, so nothing needs switching on. Put instructions and tools first and anything that changes last, then check the cached tokens in usage. Use the 12-hour lifetime only where requests are hours apart.
change_recipe.left_off: Nothing else changes; the new path sits behind a setting until a person turns it on

gain_independent: Deriv's engineers, on their own production agent: an 85.8% cache-hit rate cut input-token costs 77%, after restructuring prompts. That's input tokens only, and the post's dollar figures are illustrative; it doesn't say which provider that agent runs on.
